summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes and gastroparesis was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain and nausea, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had elevated white blood cell count without signs of infection and was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and oral pain medications. Her blood glucose was monitored closely, and her glargine insulin dose was temporarily reduced. Blood pressure and heart rate were controlled with atenolol, lisinopril, and nifedipine. She improved over 24 hours, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with her baseline medications and a plan for GI follow-up. An emergency treatment protocol was established to streamline future care.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
